translation_en: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib informed me, from his father, who said: When death came to Abu Talib, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to him and found Abu Jahl and ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah with him. He said, ‘Uncle, say, “There is no god but Allah,” a word by which I can plead for you before Allah.’ Abu Jahl and ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah said, ‘Will you turn away from the religion of ‘Abd al-Muttalib?’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, continued presenting the words to him, while they repeated that statement, until Abu Talib’s last words to them were, ‘I remain upon the religion of ‘Abd al-Muttalib,’ and he refused to say, ‘There is no god but Allah.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘By Allah, I will surely seek forgiveness for you unless I am forbidden to do so.’ Then Allah revealed, ‘It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists…’ (9:113). Allah also revealed concerning Abu Talib to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, ‘You cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills’ (28:56). Ibn ‘Abbas said: ‘Possessing strength’ (28:76) means that a group of men could not lift it. ‘It would weigh heavily’ means it would burden them. ‘Empty’ means empty except for the remembrance of Musa. ‘Those who exult’ means those who are arrogant. ‘Follow her tracks’ (28:11) means follow his trail. The word ‘qas’ can also mean recounting speech, as in, ‘We recount to you’ (18:13). ‘From afar’ (28:11) means from a distance; it can also mean from the side, or from avoiding something. ‘Yabtishu’ and ‘yabtushu’ are both forms meaning to seize. ‘They conferred’ means they consulted one another. ‘Transgression,’ ‘hostility,’ and ‘overstepping’ have the same meaning. ‘He perceived’ means he saw. A ‘burning brand’ is a thick piece of wood without a flame, whereas a flame-bearing meteor has a flame. ‘Serpents’ is a general term; the jinn-serpent, vipers, and dark snakes are kinds of them. ‘A support’ means a helper. Ibn ‘Abbas said: ‘He will confirm me.’ Another said: ‘We will strengthen you’ means, ‘We will help you’; whenever you strengthen something, you give it a support. ‘Disgraced’ means destroyed. ‘We connected it’ means We made it clear and completed it. ‘It is brought’ means it is brought in. ‘It became insolent’ means it exulted arrogantly. ‘In its mother city’ (28:59) means in the Mother of Cities, Makkah, and its surrounding area. ‘What they conceal’ means what they hide. ‘I concealed a thing’ means I hid it; ‘kanantuhu’ can mean I hid it, or I made it appear. ‘Woe to you! Do you not see that Allah…’ (28:82) has the sense of ‘Do you not see that Allah…’ (13:26): He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills.

Al-Humaydi narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: ‘Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali narrated to me that he heard ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi‘, ‘Ali’s scribe, say: I heard ‘Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sent me, al-Zubayr, and al-Miqdad and said, ‘Go until you reach the garden of Khakh. There is a woman traveling there with a letter; take it from her.’ We set out, our horses carrying us swiftly, until we reached the garden. There we found the woman traveling. We said, ‘Take out the letter.’ She said, ‘I have no letter with me.’ We said, ‘You will take out the letter, or we will remove your clothes.’ She took it out from her braided hair. We brought it to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and it was a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta‘ah to some polytheists in Makkah, informing them of some of the Prophet’s plans. The Prophet said, ‘What is this, Hatib?’ He replied, ‘Do not be hasty with me, Messenger of Allah. I was a man from Quraysh, but I was not one of their own families. The Emigrants who are with you have relatives who protect their families and property in Makkah. Since I lacked the lineage ties they have, I wanted to gain a favor with them so that they would protect my relatives. I did not do this out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘He has told you the truth.’ ‘Umar said, ‘Messenger of Allah, let me strike his neck.’ He replied, ‘He was present at Badr. How do you know? Perhaps Allah, Mighty and Majestic, looked at the people of Badr and said, “Do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.”’ ‘Amr said: The verse, ‘O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies…’ (60:1), was revealed concerning him. I do not know whether the verse was part of the hadith or whether those were ‘Amr’s words. ‘Ali narrated to us: Sufyan was asked about this wording, ‘Then “Do not take My enemy…” (60:1) was revealed.’ Sufyan said, ‘This is in the people’s narration. I memorized it from ‘Amr, and I have not left out a single letter of it. I do not think anyone else memorized it.’
